title: Disease and disorder management — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define the source-supported claims and explicit evidence boundaries required before authoring the full controlled GROW-100 SOP package.

included: Botrytis and other bud-rot differential context
excludedUntilFacilityValidated: fixed environmental setpoints presented as cannabis-wide disease-prevention guarantees

claims.statement: Cannabis root and crown disease can involve Fusarium and Pythium species, with signs such as root browning, crown/stem discoloration, stunting or yellowing; waterlogging can create overlapping root symptoms, so direct pathogen diagnosis matters.
claims.boundary: Symptoms alone do not establish species identity or distinguish every abiotic root disorder.

claims.statement: Powdery mildew and Botrytis bud rot are documented important diseases of greenhouse cannabis, while other fungal organisms can also affect inflorescences and postharvest quality.
claims.boundary: Visible white growth or bud discoloration must not be treated as species-level confirmation when look-alikes are plausible.

claims.statement: HLVd can occur in cannabis stock/propagation material and infection may be asymptomatic; infected stock can contribute to reduced rooting/vigor and downstream crop effects.
claims.boundary: Absence of visible dudding or distortion does not establish HLVd-free status.

claims.statement: Molecular diagnostic methods are important for cannabis pathogen and viroid detection when visual evidence is insufficient or consequences of misdiagnosis are high.
claims.boundary: The course may explain diagnostic strategy but must not claim a facility assay is validated without specimen, method, controls, laboratory and performance evidence.

claims.statement: HLVd has documented routes of persistence and spread relevant to propagation and hydroponic production, supporting clean-stock, movement-control and contamination-pathway review.
claims.boundary: Published experimental conditions do not justify copying a disinfection recipe or assuming the same efficacy in another facility.

claims.statement: Integrated cannabis disease management combines pathogen-free/clean stock, sanitation, monitoring, irrigation/root-zone management, environmental/cultural controls, and appropriately authorized biological or other interventions.
claims.boundary: Product legality, label directions, efficacy and worker/environmental safety require current jurisdiction- and facility-specific verification.

claims.statement: A defensible disease workup separates direct observations, spatial/temporal patterns and contextual facts from hypotheses, then uses consequence-proportional confirmation before high-impact action.
claims.boundary: This evidence framework does not replace a qualified plant pathologist or accredited/validated laboratory where confirmation is required.

releaseGates: facility/jurisdiction-specific legal and pesticide-label review where applicable
